- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for next 3–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 2x recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 20–40% for 2–4 days post-spike.  
- If forecast mean is > 1.5x true mean over 30d, apply “mean reversion” — subtract 0.1–0.3 from daily forecast for 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, -0.33, 0.67), model tends to “overfit” to recent sentiment; dampen forecast by 15–25% for next 7 days.  
- For 30d forecasts, if first 5 days show high volatility or extreme values, reduce forecast magnitude by 20–30% to avoid “over-optimism” bias.
